The pharmacist calls Paige's self-mixed taste test double-blind, and the final plan has Eshal label the cups and hand them out herself. A person who knows the codes and gives out the samples makes the test single-blind, not double-blind.

The 'second test' is just moving week-old cups around for ten minutes, and the judge accepts it as replication proving the hypothesis wrong. A ten-minute rearrangement cannot test plant growth; repeating the experiment means rerunning the full growth trial.
Aviana solves 4(x + 1) = 20 and gets three, and it 'checks'. 4x + 4 = 20 gives 4x = 16, so x = 4.

His spelling of 'perseverance' as given is already correct, yet he is said to have left out an E and then fixes it by restarting. Under Scripps rules (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scripps_National_Spelling_Bee), changing letters after restarting is a misspelling, so the ending contradicts the rule the story states.

The model shows the tilted globe with one whole hemisphere (Australia) in darkness at one side of the orbit. Tilt changes the angle of sunlight and the length of the day; it does not put a hemisphere in shadow. The lamp lights the half facing it whatever the tilt.

Rotating a square a quarter turn is said to fix the crane's folds because of paper grain. A crane's crease pattern uses both directions the same way, so a 90-degree turn changes nothing; the fix shown is false.
